instruction cache: code is assumed resident in the L1 instruction cache (steady-state hot region)

a taken forward branch, call or return costs the core 1 issue cycle(s) for the prefetch-buffer refill (R02 ch.4; S8-01 C10 fixed-direction row at four threads); loop back-edges pay nothing (S8-01 C9 at two threads); hidden at one thread by the same-context spacing
register results are available to any context's dependent instruction exactly latency cycles after issue; no bypass penalties beyond the measured latencies

x87 instructions issue on U only (register-file diagram, R01) and alone (S12-31); a memory-operand x87 load or arithmetic instruction holds its context until its result is complete; x87 stores retire like scalar stores

out-of-range or NaN double-to-int conversion produced the x86 integer indefinite; KNC-specific value not verified
ZF/SF after imul are architecturally undefined; the model leaves them unchanged
line_tracking: true LRU replacement stands in for the hardware's pseudo-LRU; the L1 and L2 are modeled as private to the core with no coherence traffic
TLB sub-model: 64-entry fully associative LRU first-level DTLB for 4096-byte pages; a miss adds 29 cycles; second-level TLB reach and page walks are not modeled

L2 hardware prefetcher sub-model: a stream per 4 KiB page after two accesses with the same stride (<= 2 lines), prefetching 16 lines ahead within the page into L2; prefetched fills do not use L1 demand-miss slots (assumed)
memory service sub-model: one memory fill per 20 core cycles for this core (measured sequential-stream rate, includes the hardware prefetcher); card-level sharing not modeled

front end: instruction bytes come from the listing; each two-cycle prefix (66, 67, lock, segment, rep: R02 p.56) delays that instruction's issue to 2 cycles per prefix after the previous issue of its context, which the 2-cycle same-context spacing hides for one prefix (S12-31 padding rows); an instruction with such a prefix does not pair (assumed)
front end: crossing a 16-byte or 64-byte boundary and the loop-head offset cost nothing (S12-31 mis_4..mis_60 within 0.45 ns per row)
instruction cache: code is assumed resident in the L1 instruction cache (steady-state hot region)

a taken forward branch, call or return costs the core 1 issue cycle(s) for the prefetch-buffer refill (R02 ch.4; S8-01 C10 fixed-direction row at four threads); loop back-edges pay nothing (S8-01 C9 at two threads); hidden at one thread by the same-context spacing
register results are available to any context's dependent instruction exactly latency cycles after issue; no bypass penalties beyond the measured latencies

x87 instructions issue on U only (register-file diagram, R01) and alone (S12-31); a memory-operand x87 load or arithmetic instruction holds its context until its result is complete; x87 stores retire like scalar stores
load-to-use beyond L1 = level latency + (L1 form latency - scalar L1 latency); the extra form cost is assumed additive
sign/zero extensions (movslq, movs*, movz*, cltq) cost a plain mov or scalar load plus latency.scalar_extend_extra and pair per pairing.extend_v_pairs: evidence E, inferred, no KNC source

calibration_status.note: Simulated/analytical outputs are model results, never native measurements.
calibration_status.statement: Core timing is inherited from core-x100-measured (measured or derived on this card: S6-03, S8-01, S8-12, S12-31). Predictions were compared with 119 characterization rows (held-out median error 0.9/0.4/1.6% at 1/2/4 threads, ranking 0.989) and with 105 held-out compiled rows from the binaries that ran on the card (S12-31 row loops, HPCG kernels L2-resident and memory-bound, S12-30 sparse products): median error 3.1%, right winner 39 of 39 pairs more than 5% apart. The decision bar's error and ranking criteria are met; its breadth (loops from at least five M4 programs) is not: shapes outside validated_shapes are unvalidated_scenario_estimate. Recording run of the final engine (profile hash 2058f0ec...).

core.min_issue_gap_same_context.source: R02 ch.4 (page locator missing): one context never issues in two consecutive cycles; R01 pp.19, 23-24 (same fact, docs/research/knc-machine.yaml thread_issue_interval); R17 slide 11; consistent with S6-03 measured 2.08 ticks per independent op at one thread
core.min_issue_gap_same_context.unit: cycles between two issue events of one context

frontend.slow_prefix_decode_cycles.source: R02 p.56 (prefix decode): 62, c4/c5, REX and 0f prefixes decode with no penalty; 66, 67, lock, segment and rep prefixes take two cycles each

frontend.taken_branch_core_bubble_cycles.source: S8-01 C10 fixed-direction row: 6.22 per branch at one thread, 17.02 at four (three issues plus about one core cycle per unit); R02 ch.4 one-clock refill bubble. Hidden at one thread by the same-context spacing. Scope: forward transfers only (S8-01 C9 register chains at two threads show no cost for the loop back-edge).
frontend.taken_branch_core_bubble_cycles.unit: core issue cycles lost after a taken branch

l1.accesses_per_cycle.source: R17 slide 13 (one L1 access per cycle, load or store)
l1.accesses_per_cycle.unit: L1 data accesses per core cycle (loads and stores, not prefetches)

l1.demand_load_miss_stalls_context.source: R08 cache performance notes ('In-order design stalls thread on L1 Data Cache Misses (except for store misses); other threads on the same core can continue'); R02 ch.4 (thread-specific flush on a miss)

l1.outstanding_demand_misses_per_core.source: R08 concurrency slide ('each core can only support 8 outstanding L1 Data Cache misses')

l1.store_miss_stalls_context.source: S6-03 l2.store_normal 23.39 ticks per store at one thread (an L2-resident footprint): each store waits for its line; R08's 'except store misses' does not hold for this card/pattern

l2.hw_prefetch_depth_lines.source: S6-03 memory.load_rt 37.35 ticks per sequential line at one thread with the hardware prefetcher active: the HWP sub-model reproduces 37.4 with depth 16 (40.2 at 12, 51.4 at 8); at four threads it gives 85.5 against 77.9 (see references/validation.md)

l2.hw_prefetch_max_stride_lines.source: R08 ('identifies strides up to 2 cache lines')

l2.hw_prefetch_streams.source: R01 p.19 (16-stream L2 hardware prefetcher, 4 KiB bounded)

l2.hw_prefetch_trains_on_stores.source: R01 TUNE_PREFQ bits (separate enables for non-RFO data reads and RFO/store reads) show the L2 prefetcher tracks store streams

latency.agi_cycles.source: S6-03 agi.gap0 3.11 vs 2.08 baseline at one thread: the dependent load issued one cycle after its earliest slot, i.e. address usable 3 cycles after the write issued; R01 p.19

latency.branch_taken_bubble.source: S8-01 C9: loop costs about 2 ticks per vector op plus 2 per loop branch at one thread (the branch costs its issue slot only)

latency.l2_hit.source: S6-03 l2.load_lat 24.42 (one thread), 25.68 at four threads

latency.mask_op.source: S6-03 kand.lat 2.08 bounds it at <=2; 1 assumed like scalar

latency.memory.source: S6-03 memory.load_lat 356.53 per dependent hop at one thread (idle) minus the first-level TLB miss of 29 cycles (tlb.l1_miss_penalty_cycles): the measured chain touches a new 4 KiB page at every hop and the TLB sub-model charges that miss explicitly. 0.2.x used 357 and double-counted it when the TLB was modeled.

latency.scalar_extend_extra.source: evidence E (estimate), inferred: plain integer sign- or zero-extension costs what mov does; no KNC source (R02 p.34 Table 3-1 lists no MOVSX/MOVZX; never measured on the card). Lead decision 2026-11-15.
latency.scalar_extend_extra.unit: cycles added to the plain mov/ALU (register form) or scalar load (memory form) latency of movslq, movs*, movz*, cltq, cltd, cqto

latency.store_to_load_same_line.source: S8-12 C9 memory chain u1 11.07 per link = folded-load add (4) + store-to-load path; spill_reload.lat 12.11 = path + plain load (5)
latency.store_to_load_same_line.unit: cycles after a store issues before a load of the same line sees the data

latency.vector_arith.source: S6-03 vaddps.lat 4.02, vmulps.lat 4.03, vfmadd213ps.lat 4.02, vpaddd.lat 4.03, vpxord.lat 4.03, vaddpd/vmulpd/vfmadd213pd 4.03, vcvtfxpntdq2ps/ps2dq 4.03

latency.vector_load_l1.source: S6-03 spill_reload.lat 12.11 = store-to-load path (7, from c9.memory.u1) + load-to-use; R08 documents 3 for vector loads
latency.vector_load_l1.unit: cycles, L1 hit plain vector load to dependent use

latency.x87_control.source: prior from the published Pentium (P5) instruction timings (FLDCW 7 clocks; FNSTCW and FNSTSW are 2). Not measured on KNC; all three are charged the FLDCW value.

latency.x87_load.source: S12-31 gas_0 488.9 and adj_0 433.5 cycles per 27-product row fix the sum of this value and the fmull memory form (operand read plus multiply) at 7 cycles; the split 3 + (1 + 3) keeps the measured x87 multiply latency of 3 and the documented one-cycle scalar load (R08)
latency.x87_load.unit: cycles from issue until the loaded value is on the x87 stack

latency.x87_move.source: evidence E (estimate), inferred: same pipeline as the measured x87 add (S6-03 x87_add.lat 3.02), no KNC source for fld/fst/fxch/fldz; fld from memory uses the load latency instead

memory.core_service_cycles_per_line.source: S6-03 memory.load_rt per core at four threads 19.48 ticks per line (37.35 at one thread); modeled as the integer 20
memory.core_service_cycles_per_line.unit: core cycles between memory fills for one core (sequential stream, hardware prefetcher active)

pairing.dependent_pairs_allowed.source: R02 p.56 (cmp/jcc, push/push, pop/pop); push/pop not modeled
pairing.dependent_pairs_allowed.unit: U/V pairs allowed despite a flag dependency

pairing.extend_v_pairs.source: evidence E (estimate), inferred: treated like the other scalar integer ops of R02 p.34 Table 3-1, which does not list them; no KNC source. Lead decision 2026-11-15.
pairing.extend_v_pairs.unit: boolean: may movslq, movs*, movz*, cltq, cltd, cqto issue in the V slot

pairing.load_store_pair.source: S6-03 spill_reload.rt at four threads: 1.07 core cycles per vector store plus reload, so a U-pipe load and a V-pipe store issue in one cycle; the L1 access limit is applied to loads only

pairing.u_instruction_can_be_branch.source: evidence E (estimate), model assumption without a KNC source: an instruction after a control transfer in the same issue slot is not paired

pairing.u_nop_pairs.source: S6-03 agi.gap1-4: each nop beyond the first costs a full issue slot (4.15, 6.16, 8.18, 10.19 ticks), so nop+nop never pair; a nop still fills a V slot
pairing.u_nop_pairs.unit: boolean: may a nop in the U slot take a V partner

pairing.v_eligible_classes.source: R02 p.34 Table 3-1 (mask, vector store, packstore, prefetch, scalar); R17 slide 10 (scalar dual issue)
pairing.v_eligible_classes.unit: instruction classes that may issue on the V pipe

pairing.v_jmp_pairs.source: S8-01 C10 fixed-direction row: cmp/je, add, jmp cost three issue events per unit (6.22 ticks at one thread), so the jmp did not pair with the add; conditional branches keep the cmp/jcc pairing (R02 p.56)
pairing.v_jmp_pairs.unit: boolean: may an unconditional jmp issue in the V slot

pairing.v_nop_pairs.source: S12-31 microbench window 5: fifteen single-byte NOPs before the loop cost 22.7 ns per row, 1.51 ns (one issue) each; S6-03 agi.gap1-4 for the U side

pairing.x87_pairs_with_scalar.source: S12-31 microbench, card windows 3 and 5 (2026-11-15): moving faddp out from between cmp and jg saves one issue per iteration (adj_0 and mid_0 -44.8/-45.6 ns per 27-product row, 1.66 ns per iteration); an x87 instruction issues alone

store.load_after_store_interlock_cycles.source: S6-03 spill_reload.rt 4.20/4.26 per pair at two/four threads and S8-12 C9 memory chains u2/u4 8.56/8.30 per link at one thread (two issues plus four cycles); vector rows only, applied to scalar stores as well (assumed)
store.load_after_store_interlock_cycles.unit: cycles after a store before the same context may issue a load

tlb.l1_entries_4k.source: S8-12 C4 rerun (2026-11-08): loads cost L1 latency up to 64 4 KiB pages per core and about 29 ticks more beyond

tlb.l1_miss_penalty_cycles.source: S8-12 C4 rerun: 31.76-31.79 vs 3.01-3.02 ticks per load at one thread

x87.mem_operand_serializes.source: S12-31 microbench (card windows 3 and 5): the row loop costs two cycles per issue plus a constant whatever follows fmull (faddp directly, or add and cmp first), so the instructions after an x87 memory-operand instruction do not issue while it completes
